beats.say: In 1821 Mexico emerges from Spanish rule, inheriting vast northern territories stretching to present-day Texas.
1845 sees the Republic of Texas vote for U.S. annexation, inflaming border disputes with Mexico.
In 1846 the United States declares war on Mexico, eyes the disputed Texas border.
At Buena Vista in February 1847, General Zachary Taylor halts Santa Anna's advance, securing a tactical victory.
September 1847 sees U.S. forces under Winfield Scott storm Mexico City, forcing the capital's surrender.
The 1848 Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo redraws the map, ceding California, New Mexico, Utah and more to America.
This conflict fuels Manifest Destiny, proving a war can legitimize continental ambition and future overseas ventures.
Even after defeat, Mexican guerrillas wage resistance in the Sierra Madre, refusing full surrender.
